metadata.title: SecOps-NG — DORA ICT Risk Management & Incident Reporting Component Definition (EXTEND)

components.title: SecOps-NG
components.description: SecOps-NG is a community-driven Digital Commons of portable security operations content (CACAO playbooks, OSCAL/D3FEND control mappings, OCSF data shapes, KPI/KRI catalog) plus reference compilers to n8n, Temporal, and LangGraph. This component definition exposes how the SecOps-NG content set addresses the DORA ICT risk-management framework (Chapter II) and ICT-related incident management, classification, and reporting (Chapter III) obligations.

control-implementations.description: Coverage of DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) Chapter II ICT risk-management framework obligations — Article 5 governance and organisation, Article 6 ICT risk-management framework, Article 7 ICT systems, protocols and tools, Article 8 identification, Article 9 vulnerability and patch management, Article 10 detection, Article 11 response and recovery, Article 12 backup policies and restoration, Article 13 learning and evolving (post-incident review), and Article 14 crisis communication — together with Chapter III ICT-related incident classification and reporting obligations (Articles 18–19), as mapped in content/mappings/dora/article-5.yaml, article-6.yaml, article-7.yaml, article-8.yaml, article-9-and-rts-vuln-mgmt.yaml, article-10.yaml, article-11.yaml, article-12.yaml, article-13.yaml, article-14.yaml, and article-19-and-28.yaml. Third-party-risk obligations (Articles 28+) remain out of scope for this layer.

implemented-requirements.description: Establish an internal governance and control framework that ensures effective and prudent management of ICT risk, with the management body bearing ultimate responsibility for the ICT risk-management framework, setting roles and responsibilities for ICT functions, and approving and reviewing the framework at least annually.

Establish an internal governance and control framework that ensures effective and prudent management of ICT risk, with the management body bearing ultimate responsibility for the ICT risk-management framework, setting roles and responsibilities for ICT functions, and approving and reviewing the framework at least annually.

Establish, document and maintain a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk-management framework that is part of the overall risk-management system, is reviewed at least annually and upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents, and is subject to audit by ICT auditors on a regular basis.

Use ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate to the magnitude of operations supporting the conduct of activities, reliable, equipped with sufficient capacity to accurately process data, and technologically resilient so as to adequately deal with additional information processing needs required by stressed market conditions or other adverse situations.

Have in place mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, and to identify potential material single points of failure, with multiple layers of control, defined alert thresholds and criteria to trigger ICT-related incident detection and response processes, including automatic alert mechanisms for relevant staff.

Develop and document backup policies and procedures specifying the scope of the data subject to backup and the minimum frequency, together with restoration and recovery procedures and methods that ensure restoration of ICT systems and data with minimum downtime and limited disruption, with periodic testing of those backup, restoration, and recovery procedures.

Have in place capabilities and staff to gather information on vulnerabilities and cyber threats, ICT-related incidents (in particular cyber-attacks), and analyse their likely impacts on digital operational resilience; conduct post-ICT-related incident reviews after a major ICT-related incident disrupts core activities, analysing the causes of disruption and identifying required improvements to the ICT operations or to the ICT business continuity policy.

Have in place crisis communication plans enabling a responsible disclosure of, at least, major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and the public as appropriate, and implement communication policies for staff and external stakeholders that distinguish between those responsible for managing ICT-related incidents externally and internally, with at least one person tasked with implementing the communication strategy for ICT-related incidents and fulfilling the public and media function for that purpose.

Develop, document and implement vulnerability and patch management procedures covering identification of vulnerabilities in ICT assets (including automated vulnerability scanning where appropriate), monitoring of third-party vendor and library disclosures and CVE feeds, risk-based prioritisation and remediation deadlines, tracking of remediation status to closure, and a patch management procedure including testing and rollback.

Classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact based on the criteria specified in Article 18(1) and operationalised by the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 (seven primary criteria plus materiality thresholds; recurring-incident rule).

Submit an initial notification of a major ICT-related incident to the competent authority within the deadlines set by the Commission ITS — as soon as possible, within 4 hours of classification as major, and no later than 24 hours from awareness.

Submit an intermediate report within 72 hours of classification of the incident as major (or earlier if regular activities have recovered), updating timestamps, affected functions and clients, indicators of compromise, and mitigation actions in flight.

Submit a final report no later than one month after submission of the intermediate report, containing the full root-cause analysis, final impact figures, completed remediation actions, lessons learned, action plan, and residual-risk statement.

Voluntary notification of significant cyber threats to the competent authority, with content shape defined by the relevant ESAs RTS/ITS. No mandatory clock; lighter content schema than a major-incident notification.
Treat as a major incident any series of recurring incidents that share the same apparent root cause across a six-month rolling window and, in aggregate, exceed the materiality thresholds.
